newsitem.title: USA: Former mayor says he unseated Republican congressman.
newsitem.headline: Former mayor says he unseated Republican congressman.

text.p: Cleveland's one-time "boy mayor," Democrat Dennis Kucinich, claimed victory early on Wednesday in a tight race against two-term Republican Martin Hoke.
With 98 percent of the vote counted, Kucinich had 49.0 percent to Hoke's 46.4 percent, local elections officials said. Natural Law candidate Robert Iverson had 4.6 percent.
Kucinich credited his diverse grass-roots support.

"The reason why we won today is because we had a powerful grass roots operation (of) thousands of volunteers," he told supporters at his victory party in a speech broadcast by WMJI radio. "We won this election house to house, block by block."
Kucinich, 50, now a state senator, focused his campaign on Hoke's support of House Speaker Newt Gingrich but the two sparred on many issues.
In television ads, Hoke, 44, reminded voters Kucinich was mayor of Cleveland in 1978 when it became the first major U.S. city since the Great Depression to default on bank loans.
Ousted after one two-year term as mayor, Kucinich has said the default stemmed from the banks' displeasure with his dogged refusal to sell the city's municipal power system, which it still owns.

The 10th district, which includes Cleveland's blue collar west side and several upscale suburbs, lies mainly in Cuyahoga County, where voter turnout was lighter than expected, Board of Elections director Bill Wilkins said.
